blocks.text: Scleral lenses generally have an expected lifespan of one to two years, though some may last longer. The actual lifespan can vary based on factors such as the lens brand, material, and personal circumstances. This is general information and not a fixed replacement deadline for every patient.

Reasons a scleral lens might need replacement include deposit accumulation, damage like surface cracking or breakage, and changes in lens fit or prescription power. The surfaces of gas-permeable scleral lenses can deteriorate over time due to repeated wearing and handling. Careful handling of scleral lenses can help preserve their surface.

If you notice changes in lens fit or vision, if your lenses repeatedly shift out of place, or if they become difficult to remove, it is important to inform your eye-care provider. Your eye-care provider will recommend follow-up visits and their schedule.

# Reasons a scleral lens may need replacement

Status: Assistant-prepared paraphrase of a professional clinical article; clinical review pending. This is professional guidance, not a randomized study.
Prepared and source accessed: 3 October 2026.

The clinical article identifies deposit accumulation, damage such as surface cracking or breakage, and altered lens fit or prescription power as reasons a scleral lens may need replacing.

A replacement is not necessarily an identical copy. Depending on the case, the existing design may be duplicated, adjusted, or replaced through a new fitting. Changes in an ectatic cornea can alter the clearance beneath a scleral lens.

Source: Dr. DeNaeyer, Replacing and Refitting Scleral Contact Lenses, Contact Lens Spectrum, 1 November 2018.
https://www.clspectrum.com/issues/2018/november/the-scleral-lens-vault/

Source caveat: The article dates from 2018 and discloses the author's commercial interests in lens-related companies.

blocks.text: Scleral lenses are an important vision correction option for many, especially those with conditions like keratoconus. Understanding their typical lifespan and when they might need replacement can help you maintain optimal vision and comfort.

Generally, scleral lenses have an expected lifespan of one to two years, though some individuals may find their lenses last longer. It is important to remember that this is general information and not a fixed replacement deadline for every patient.

The actual lifespan of your scleral lenses can vary. Factors such as the specific lens brand, the material they are made from, and your personal circumstances can all influence how long your lenses remain effective.

There are several reasons why a scleral lens might need to be replaced. These can include the accumulation of deposits on the lens surface, damage such as surface cracking or breakage, or changes in the lens fit or your prescription power.

The surfaces of gas-permeable scleral lenses can deteriorate over time due to repeated wearing and handling. Careful handling of your scleral lenses can help preserve their surface and potentially extend their usability.

It is important to inform your eye-care provider if you notice any changes in lens fit or vision. You should also contact them if your lenses repeatedly shift out of place or become difficult to remove. Your eye-care provider will recommend follow-up visits and their schedule to monitor your eye health and lens performance.
Call +91 8247710054 to book an appointment

rejected_draft.headline: Understanding the Lifespan and Replacement of Scleral Lenses

blocks.text: Scleral lenses are an important vision correction option for many, especially those with conditions like keratoconus. Understanding their typical lifespan and when they might need replacement can help you maintain optimal vision and comfort.

Generally, scleral lenses have an expected lifespan of one to two years, though some individuals may find their lenses last longer. It's important to remember that this is general information and not a strict deadline for replacement for every patient.
The actual lifespan of your scleral lenses can vary due to several factors, including the specific lens brand, the material they are made from, and your personal circumstances.

There are several reasons why a scleral lens might need to be replaced. These can include the accumulation of deposits on the lens surface, damage such as surface cracking or breakage, or changes in the lens fit or your prescription power.

The surfaces of gas-permeable scleral lenses can naturally deteriorate over time due to repeated wearing and handling. However, careful handling of your scleral lenses can help to preserve their surface and potentially extend their usability.

It is crucial to inform your eye-care provider if you notice any changes in how your lenses fit or in your vision. You should also contact them if your lenses repeatedly shift out of place or become difficult to remove. Your eye-care provider will recommend follow-up visits and their schedule to monitor your eye health and lens condition.
Call +91 8247710054 to book an appointment

sources.text:
# Scleral lens lifespan and follow-up

Status: Assistant-prepared paraphrase of medically reviewed hospital patient information; clinical review of this summary pending.
Prepared and source accessed: 3 October 2026.

Cleveland Clinic gives one to two years as a general expected lifespan for scleral lenses, while noting that some last longer. An individual's expected lifespan depends on factors such as lens brand, material and personal circumstances. This is general information, not a fixed replacement deadline for every patient.

Cleveland Clinic advises telling an eye-care provider about changes in lens fit or vision, lenses that repeatedly shift out of place, or lenses that become difficult to remove. Follow-up visits and their schedule are recommended by the eye-care provider.

sources.text:
# Reasons a scleral lens may need replacement

Status: Assistant-prepared paraphrase of a professional clinical article; clinical review pending. This is professional guidance, not a randomized study.
Prepared and source accessed: 3 October 2026.

The clinical article identifies deposit accumulation, damage such as surface cracking or breakage, and altered lens fit or prescription power as reasons a scleral lens may need replacing.

A replacement is not necessarily an identical copy. Depending on the case, the existing design may be duplicated, adjusted, or replaced through a new fitting. Changes in an ectatic cornea can alter the clearance beneath a scleral lens.

Source: Dr. DeNaeyer, Replacing and Refitting Scleral Contact Lenses, Contact Lens Spectrum, 1 November 2018.
https://www.clspectrum.com/issues/2018/november/the-scleral-lens-vault/

Source caveat: The article dates from 2018 and discloses the author's commercial interests in lens-related companies.

sources.text:
# Scleral lens surface wear

Status: Assistant-prepared paraphrase of hospital patient guidance; clinical review pending.
Prepared and source accessed: 3 October 2026.

Moorfields Eye Hospital explains that the surfaces of gas-permeable scleral lenses can deteriorate through repeated wearing and handling. Re-polishing a lens is not always an option. Careful handling helps preserve the lens surface.

Source: Moorfields Eye Hospital, Care of your scleral contact lenses, section Taking care of your contact lenses.
https://www.moorfields.nhs.uk/for-patients/visual-aids/contact-lenses/care-of-your-scleral-contact-lenses

Scope: Explains surface wear. This source does not establish an individual replacement date or a clinic's replacement policy.
